In summary, our research is concerned with
the recognition of target cells by NK cells.
the identification of the target structures for human NK cells and with the characterization of the human NK cell system.
the identification of the target cells for human NK cells, the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms involved, and the development of NK cells for clinical applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

human NK cells are not only capable of recognizing and destroying tumor cells but also have the capacity for recognizing and destroying autologous and/or allogeneic normal lymphocytes and that the NK cell population is heterogeneous with regard to its cytolytic activity against various target cells.

natural killer cells recognize and kill autologous and/or allogeneic target cells that are either FcR1- and/or FcR11-negative, and that are not HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, HLA-DP, HLA-B, HLA-C, HLA-A, HLA-A2 or HLA-B7 positive.

NK cells can be divided into two subpopulations: (i) a population of NK cells that recognize and kill only allogeneic target cells and (ii) a population that recognizes both autologous and non-autologous target cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
human natural killer (NK) cells are a subset of the FcR1-bearing lymphocytes and that they recognize a variety of cell surface structures on target cells.
human natural killer (NK) cells recognize histocompatibility antigents or related structures on target cells and the recognition is independent of HLA antigents.
human NK cells recognize a variety of target cells by different recognition mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NK cells recognize allogeneic cells and tumor cells by a mechanism that is distinct from that used for recognition of autologous lymphocytes.
NK cells can recognize and kill a variety of tumor cells, including those that are resistant to T-cell mediated killing.
the NK cell is not a monolithic population, but rather a diverse collection of cells that recognize and respond to distinct target cell types.
